meaning: as if truly ~; looking every bit as though ~ (of appearance or manner)

exercises.example_sentence: 彼はさも自分の手柄であるかのように、その成功を語った。
exercises.translation: He spoke of the success as if it had been entirely his own doing.
wrong_choice_explanations: なんとなく means 'vaguely, somehow'. なんとなく自分の手柄であるかのように softens his bragging into a faint impression, while the sentence describes him blatantly passing the success off as his own — the 'every bit as if' that さも gives.
意外と means 'surprisingly'. 意外と自分の手柄であるかのように makes no sense: nothing here is unexpected, and 意外と doesn't modify a pretence; さも marks how brazenly he acted as if it were his doing.
たいして means 'not very' and needs a negative. たいして自分の手柄であるかのように has no negative to complete it, so it breaks; さも intensifies the pretence that follows.

audio_alternatives.kanji: 彼はさも手柄顔で、その成功を自慢げに話した。

exercises.example_sentence: 猫はさも満足そうに、日なたで丸くなっていた。
exercises.translation: The cat lay curled up in the sun, looking utterly content.
wrong_choice_explanations: なんとなく means 'somehow, vaguely'. なんとなく満足そうに is natural — the cat looks faintly content — but the sentence pictures it looking utterly content, the vivid 'every bit as if' that さも adds.
どうやら marks an inference and belongs with sentence-final ようだ or らしい: どうやら満足しているようだ. It cannot modify the adverbial 満足そうに describing how the cat lay; さも intensifies that appearance.
なぜか means 'for some reason'. なぜか満足そうに is natural — the cat looked content for no clear reason — but the sentence is painting how blissful it looked, not puzzling over a cause; that emphasis is さも.

exercises.example_sentence: さも当然のような顔で、彼女は列の先頭に割り込んだ。
exercises.translation: With a look as if it were the most natural thing, she cut in at the front of the line.
wrong_choice_explanations: なんとなく means 'vaguely, somehow'. なんとなく当然のような顔 is a faint look, but she cut to the front of the line with a brazen air of entitlement — the exaggerated 'as if it were obvious' of さも.
意外と means 'surprisingly'. 意外と当然のような顔 makes no sense: nothing here contradicts an expectation; さも marks the brazen show of entitlement as she pushed in.
かえって means 'on the contrary' and needs an expectation to reverse. かえって当然のような顔 has no such contrast in the sentence; さも marks the pretended naturalness of her cutting in.

exercises.example_sentence: その男はさも親しげに私の肩を叩いたが、名前すら知らなかった。
exercises.translation: The man clapped me on the shoulder as if we were close friends, though he didn't even know my name.
wrong_choice_explanations: なんとなく means 'somehow, vaguely'. なんとなく親しげに is natural, but the point is that a stranger acted unmistakably chummy — 'as if we were close friends' — which is the exaggerated show さも describes.
なぜか means 'for some reason'. なぜか親しげに肩を叩いた is natural Japanese ('for some reason he patted me in a friendly way'); it questions his motive instead of stressing his put-on familiarity, as さも does.
たいして means 'not very' and requires a negative. たいして親しげに肩を叩いた has no negative, so it doesn't work; さも intensifies the friendly show of a man who didn't even know my name.

exercises.example_sentence: さも知っているかのように相槌を打っていたが、実は何も分かっていなかった。
exercises.translation: He nodded along as if he knew all about it, but in fact he understood nothing.
wrong_choice_explanations: なんとなく means 'somehow, vaguely'. なんとなく知っているかのように weakens the pretence, but the sentence describes him nodding along convincingly while understanding nothing — the 'as if he knew all about it' of さも.
どうやら marks an inference and ends in ようだ or らしい: どうやら知っているようだ. It cannot sit before かのように describing his manner; さも intensifies the act of seeming to know.
意外と means 'surprisingly'. 意外と知っているかのように makes no sense, since a pretence isn't something one does 'unexpectedly' here; さも marks how convincingly he faked knowing.

vocab.meaning: to nod along; to chime in

exercises.example_sentence: その子はさも痛そうに顔をしかめてみせたが、傷はどこにもなかった。
exercises.translation: The child screwed up his face as if it really hurt, but there wasn't a scratch on him.
wrong_choice_explanations: なんとなく means 'somehow, vaguely'. なんとなく痛そうに clashes with しかめてみせた, which is a deliberate performance; a put-on grimace is exaggerated, the 'as if it really hurt' that さも expresses.
なぜか means 'for some reason'. なぜか痛そうに顔をしかめてみせた is sayable, but it puzzles over why instead of describing the child's exaggerated act of pain; さも stresses the show, which the missing scratch exposes.
たいして means 'not very' and requires a negative. たいして痛そうに顔をしかめてみせた has none, so it breaks; さも intensifies how pained the child pretended to look.

exercises.example_sentence: さも重大な秘密であるかのように、彼は声をひそめて話し始めた。
exercises.translation: As if it were some grave secret, he lowered his voice and began to speak.
wrong_choice_explanations: なんとなく means 'somehow, vaguely'. なんとなく重大な秘密であるかのように undercuts the act: lowering his voice is a deliberate show of gravity, the 'as if it were some grave secret' that さも describes.
どうやら marks an inference and ends in ようだ or らしい. It cannot modify かのように describing his manner; どうやら重大な秘密であるかのように breaks, while さも intensifies the show of secrecy.
かえって means 'on the contrary' and needs an expectation to reverse. かえって重大な秘密であるかのように has no contrast to complete; さも marks the dramatic pretence of a secret.

exercises.example_sentence: 頼み事をすると、彼はさも迷惑そうにため息をついた。
exercises.translation: Whenever you asked him a favor, he would sigh as if it were the greatest nuisance.
wrong_choice_explanations: なんとなく means 'somehow, vaguely'. なんとなく迷惑そうに is natural, but the sentence portrays a pointed, theatrical sigh as if a favour were the greatest nuisance — the exaggeration さも adds.
意外と means 'surprisingly'. 意外と迷惑そうに clashes with the habitual 頼み事をすると ('whenever you asked'): a reaction he shows every time can't be unexpected; さも marks his exaggerated annoyance.
なぜか means 'for some reason'. なぜか迷惑そうに is natural ('for some reason he sighed as if annoyed'), but the favour is the obvious trigger and the sentence stresses his showy annoyance, which is さも.

exercises.example_sentence: 店員はさも申し訳なさそうに頭を下げたが、対応は一向に変わらなかった。
exercises.translation: The clerk bowed as if truly apologetic, yet nothing about the response changed at all.
wrong_choice_explanations: なんとなく means 'somehow, vaguely'. なんとなく申し訳なさそうに is natural, but the sentence contrasts a showy, apparently sincere bow with nothing changing — the 'as if truly apologetic' that さも conveys.
たいして means 'not very' and requires a negative. たいして申し訳なさそうに頭を下げた has none, so it breaks; さも intensifies how apologetic the clerk looked.
どうやら marks an inference and ends in ようだ or らしい. It cannot modify the adverbial 申し訳なさそうに describing the bow; さも intensifies the apologetic look that the unchanged response belies.

exercises.example_sentence: さも嬉しそうに尻尾を振る犬を見て、こちらまで心が和んだ。
exercises.translation: Seeing the dog wag its tail as if truly delighted, even I felt my heart soften.
wrong_choice_explanations: なんとなく means 'somehow, vaguely'. なんとなく嬉しそうに is natural, but the dog's tail-wagging is pictured as unmistakable delight that softens the speaker's heart — the vivid 'as if truly delighted' of さも.
なぜか means 'for some reason'. なぜか嬉しそうに尻尾を振る犬 is natural, but it puzzles over the cause instead of picturing the dog's obvious joy, which is what さも adds and what softens the speaker's heart.
意外と means 'surprisingly'. 意外と嬉しそうに suggests the dog wasn't expected to be happy, which nothing in the sentence sets up; さも stresses how delighted it looked.
